title: AdvDiffuser: Generating Adversarial Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios via Guided Diffusion

control_signal.value: A designer-defined adversarial reward: collision reward for the target AV minus a penalty for background-vehicle collisions (R_t = R_adv - P_coll), plus map and history context.

control_mechanism.value: A lightweight reward model's gradient refines each denoising step in latent space (guided sampling); context enters the denoiser via latent code concatenation and AdaGN. Only the reward model is adapted to new target planners.

base_model.value: Latent diffusion: GNN interaction net/context encoder, U-Net noise predictor with AdaGN, VAE-style posterior network (ELBO), autoregressive trajectory decoder with bicycle model.

datasets.value: nuScenes (1000 scenes, 20 s at 2 Hz), split into 8-second segments: 2 s history, 6 s future.

metrics.value: Diversity (minSFDE, FDD), distribution realism (JSD of velocity, acceleration, TTC), common sense (env/vehicle collision rate of background vehicles), adversarial collision rate and velocity, comfort (acceleration, jerk).

controllability_evidence.value: Packet shows only the unguided realism table: vehicle collision 0.02 % vs AdvSim 0.87 % and Strive 0.16 %. Adversarial-performance table (guided results) is not in the packet; abstract claims better realism, diversity, adversarial performance and transfer.

stated_limitations.value: Discussion notes no universally accepted benchmark for safety-critical scenarios, so the validity and real-world relevance of generated adversarial scenarios remain uncertain.

notes: Adversarial-guidance result numbers (Table II) were not in the packet; the evidence cell reports only the unguided traffic realism comparison.
